title: Rethinking Pre-training and Self-training
mechanism: A fixed teacher pseudo-labels extra data, and the student is trained on labels plus pseudo-labels under strong augmentation. Self-training helps at every label size, including 100%, when the augmentation is strong.
adaptation: Our house uses weak label-safe augmentation because hard 1-2 px labels break under resampling. Soft teacher probabilities can be resampled bilinearly, so pool images can take scale jitter 0.75-1.5, small rotation, blur and gamma. Labelled cells keep label-safe aug. Teacher = the ensemble of paper 1.
min_experiment: Arm B of the ensemble-distillation experiment, run with and without strong aug on pool images (aug ablation). Baseline: PF single model. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU and relF1@2, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: strong-aug arm not better than weak-aug arm by +0.005 crack IoU or +0.02 E1 relF1@2.
evidence: R: COCO detection, self-training +1.3 to +3.4 AP at every data size including 100% labels, while ImageNet pretraining hurt at full COCO. PASCAL segmentation +1.5 mIoU over the previous SOTA (90.5 mIoU), on top of a pretrained model.
prior_overlap: Partial. The BRIEF SSL row (Mean Teacher with CutMix, 11.9k pool, 100% labels) was n.d. That run used an online EMA teacher and weak label-safe geometry. An offline stronger teacher with soft labels and strong scale augmentation on the pool is open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Use strong geometric and photometric aug (scale jitter 0.5 to 2, elastic, blur, gamma) only on pseudo-labelled pool cells: the pseudo mask is warped with the image, so the label-safe rule for jittered GT does not apply. Use the L_h/L_p EMA normalisation (decay 0.9997). Can be combined with the Naive-Student arm.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Within the NS-12k arm, compare student aug = label-safe vs strong (5 seeds each). Metric: crack relF1@2 and IoU on clean-49, E1 relF1@2. Kill if strong aug is n.d. vs label-safe.
